findings.summary: Phase 2 no-product-web-change verifier re-evaluated descendant Phase 3 web changes as Phase 2 scope drift.
Phase 2 web guard forbade the exact preview header Phase 3 must deliberately send.
apps/api broad typecheck short-circuits on four pre-existing defense-budget TS6059 errors and suppresses later tsconfig projects.
findings.fixDecision: Phase 3 permanent verifier invokes tsconfig.engagement-phase3-fixtures.json directly; unrelated defense-budget repair remains outside Phase 3.

findings.summary: React Query cache entries did not encode response runtime provenance, allowing main/preview cache reuse and an in-flight old-mode response to populate the new mode.
findings.fixDecision: Mark actual Engagement response objects, cancel/remove only Engagement-owned queries on mode transitions, and reject any response whose dispatch-time mode no longer matches current mode.

findings.summary: Deterministic Phase 3 fixtures intentionally use synthetic Clerk identities, which cannot authenticate a real browser acceptance session.
findings.fixDecision: Keep the committed fixture contract synthetic and byte-stable; bind only Clerk identity columns to dedicated acceptance actors at runtime in the disposable database.

findings.summary: Initial Phase 3 runner design placed the temporary browser bearer-token file under the retained evidence directory.
findings.fixDecision: Bearer material lives only in the OS temp directory and is force-deleted in runner cleanup; evidence files contain sanitized headers only.
